```text
  "body": "## Summary\n\nAlmost all tables in Actual Budget support bulk editing, via selecting checkboxes. The \"schedules\" table one of the only tables in the application that does not allow for bulk editing. Checkboxes should be added to each element in the table. The user should be able to select as many scheduled transaction as they would like, and bulk edit them at once, allow for the user to post transactions, skip next scheduled date, complete, or delete. \n\n## User Story\n\nAs a user who has many bills scheduled, I want an easy way to bulk update and delete recurring bills so I do not have to manually edit each transaction at a time.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. Each element in the schedule table now has a checkbox so it can be selected.\n2. There is a checkbox to the left of the name field on the table allowing the user to select all transactions scheduled.\n3. Upon selecting at least one transaction, the user can click a bulk edit button to edit all selected transactions at once.\n4. The bulk edit menu should have options for each pre-existing edit option for an individual transaction.\n5. All selected transactions should successfully update.\n6. The user should not be able to bulk edit completed transactions.\n\n<img width=\"212\" height=\"268\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b61f5ac-e51e-4551-b90e-ddbe9faa089f\" />\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- The ability to edit completed transactions. \n- Scheduling table UI redesign outside of adding checkboxes\n- Keyboard shortcuts\n- Any new edit options for the bulk edit option menu\n\n## Open Questions\n\n1. Where should the bulk edit button be located?\n2. How should the table be redesigned to allow for new checkboxes without looking strange?\n3. What should happen if the user tries to bulk edit a completed transaction?\n\n\n## Rough Scope\n\nMedium -- requires a frontend UI redesign to preexisting components, as well as backend logic to ensure bulk edits apply appropriately to each transaction. Pre-existing bulk-edit logic exists widely in the codebase so is nothing new, and can be used for reference, so not marking as a large issue.\n\n## Source\n\nPersonally playing around with the application.",
```

```text
import React, { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import { ErrorBoundary } from 'react-error-boundary';
import { Trans, useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';

import { Button } from '@actual-app/components/button';
import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';
import { send } from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
import { q } from '@actual-app/core/shared/query';
import type { ScheduleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { Search } from '#components/common/Search';
import { FeatureErrorFallback } from '#components/FeatureErrorFallback';
import { Page } from '#components/Page';
import { useSchedules } from '#hooks/useSchedules';
import { useSearchHotkey } from '#hooks/useSearchHotkey';
import { pushModal } from '#modals/modalsSlice';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

import { SchedulesTable } from './SchedulesTable';
import type { ScheduleItemAction } from './SchedulesTable';

export function Schedules() {
  const { t } = useTranslation();

  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('');
  const searchInput = useSearchHotkey();

  const onEdit = useCallback(
    (id: ScheduleEntity['id']) => {
      dispatch(
        pushModal({ modal: { name: 'schedule-edit', options: { id } } }),
      );
    },
    [dispatch],
  );

  const onAdd = useCallback(() => {
    dispatch(pushModal({ modal: { name: 'schedule-edit', options: {} } }));
  }, [dispatch]);

  const onDiscover = useCallback(() => {
    dispatch(pushModal({ modal: { name: 'schedules-discover' } }));
  }, [dispatch]);

  const onChangeUpcomingLength = useCallback(() => {
    dispatch(pushModal({ modal: { name: 'schedules-upcoming-length' } }));
  }, [dispatch]);

  const onAction = useCallback(
    async (name: ScheduleItemAction, id: ScheduleEntity['id']) => {
      switch (name) {
        case 'post-transaction':
          await send('schedule/post-transaction', { id });
          break;
        case 'post-transaction-today':
          await send('schedule/post-transaction', { id, today: true });
          break;
        case 'skip':
          await send('schedule/skip-next-date', { id });
          break;
        case 'complete':
          await send('schedule/update', {
            schedule: { id, completed: true },
          });
          break;
        case 'restart':
          await send('schedule/update', {
            schedule: { id, completed: false },
            resetNextDate: true,
          });
          break;
        case 'delete':
          await send('schedule/delete', { id });
          break;
        default:
          throw new Error(`Unknown action: ${String(name)}`);
      }
    },
    [],
  );

  const schedulesQuery = useMemo(() => q('schedules').select('*'), []);
  const {
    isLoading: isSchedulesLoading,
    schedules,
    statuses,
  } = useSchedules({ query: schedulesQuery });

  return (
    <ErrorBoundary FallbackComponent={FeatureErrorFallback}>
      <Page header={t('Schedules')}>
        <View
          style={{
            flexDirection: 'row',
            alignItems: 'center',
            padding: '0 0 15px',
          }}
        >
          <View
            style={{
              flex: 1,
              flexDirection: 'row',
              justifyContent: 'flex-end',
            }}
          >
            <Search
              ref={searchInput}
              placeholder={t('Filter schedules…')}
              value={filter}
              onChange={setFilter}
            />
          </View>
        </View>

        <SchedulesTable
          isLoading={isSchedulesLoading}
          schedules={schedules}
          filter={filter}
          statuses={statuses}
          allowCompleted
          onSelect={onEdit}
          onAction={onAction}
          style={{ backgroundColor: theme.tableBackground }}
        />

        <View
          style={{
            flexDirection: 'row',
            justifyContent: 'space-between',
            margin: '20px 0',
            flexShrink: 0,
          }}
        >
          <View
            style={{
              flexDirection: 'row',
              alignItems: 'center',
              gap: '1em',
            }}
          >
            <Button onPress={onDiscover}>
              <Trans>Find schedules</Trans>
            </Button>
            <Button onPress={onChangeUpcomingLength}>
              <Trans>Change upcoming length</Trans>
            </Button>
          </View>
          <Button variant="primary" onPress={onAdd}>
            <Trans>Add new schedule</Trans>
          </Button>
        </View>
      </Page>
    </ErrorBoundary>
  );
}
```

```text
function ScheduleRow({
  schedule,
  onAction,
  onSelect,
  minimal,
  statuses,
  dateFormat,
}: {
  schedule: ScheduleEntity;
  dateFormat: string;
} & Pick<
  SchedulesTableProps,
  'onSelect' | 'onAction' | 'minimal' | 'statuses'
>) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();

  const rowRef = useRef(null);
  const buttonRef = useRef(null);

  const status = statuses.get(schedule.id);
  useContextMenu({
    triggerRef: rowRef,
          },
        ]
      : [],
  });

  return (
    <Row
      ref={rowRef}
      height={ROW_HEIGHT}
      inset={15}
      onClick={() => onSelect(schedule.id)}
      style={{
        cursor: 'pointer',
        backgroundColor: theme.tableBackground,
        color: theme.tableText,
        ':hover': { backgroundColor: theme.tableRowBackgroundHover },
      }}
    >
      <Field width="flex" name="name">
        <Text
          style={
            schedule.name == null
              ? { color: theme.buttonNormalDisabledText }
              : null
          }
          title={schedule.name ? schedule.name : ''}
        >
          {schedule.name ? schedule.name : t('None')}
        </Text>
      </Field>
      <Field width="flex" name="payee">
        <DisplayId type="payees" id={schedule._payee} />
      </Field>
      <Field width="flex" name="account">
        <DisplayId type="accounts" id={schedule._account} />
      </Field>
      <Field width={110} name="date">
        {schedule.next_date
          ? monthUtilFormat(schedule.next_date, dateFormat)
          : null}
      </Field>
      <Field width={120} name="status" style={{ alignItems: 'flex-start' }}>
        <StatusBadge status={statuses.get(schedule.id)} />
      </Field>
      <ScheduleAmountCell amount={schedule._amount} op={schedule._amountOp} />
      {!minimal && (
        <Field width={80} style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>
          {schedule._date &&
            typeof schedule._date === 'object' &&
            schedule._date.frequency && (
              <SvgCheck style={{ width: 13, height: 13 }} />
            )}
        </Field>
      )}
      {!minimal && (
        <Field width={40} name="actions">
          <View>
            <Button
              ref={buttonRef}
              variant="bare"
              aria-label={t('Menu')}
              onPress={() => {
                if (rowRef.current) {

                  const clientX = rect ? rect.left : 0;
                  const clientY = rect ? rect.bottom : 0;
                  (rowRef.current as HTMLElement).dispatchEvent(
                    new MouseEvent('contextmenu', {
                      bubbles: true,
                      clientX,
                      clientY,
                    }),
                  );
                }
              }}
            >
              <SvgDotsHorizontalTriple
                width={15}
                height={15}
                style={{ transform: 'rotateZ(90deg)' }}
              />
            </Button>
          </View>
        </Field>
      )}
    </Row>
  );
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 01:24:08Z)**_

Issue #65, "Allow Bulk Editing in Schedules Tab", asks for checkboxes on schedule rows, a select-all box, and a bulk menu offering the same actions as the single-row menu (post, skip next date, complete, delete). Completed schedules shouldn't be bulk-editable. It's assigned to you and scoped as medium.

**What schedules lack that the other tables have.** Rules, Payees, Tags, Transactions and the admin User Directory all follow the same pattern; schedules doesn't use any part of it:

1. **Selection state.** The other pages create a selection with `useSelected(...)` and wrap the page in `<SelectedProvider>` (e.g. [ManageTags.tsx:44-53](components/tags/ManageTags.tsx#L44-L53), [ManageRules.tsx:164](components/ManageRules.tsx#L164)). [schedules/index.tsx](components/schedules/index.tsx) has no selection state.
2. **Checkbox cells.** Rows in the other tables render a `SelectCell` and update the selection through `useSelectedDispatch` ([RuleRow.tsx:92](components/rules/RuleRow.tsx#L92), [TagRow.tsx:149](components/tags/TagRow.tsx#L149)), and their header has a select-all cell. In [SchedulesTable.tsx](components/schedules/SchedulesTable.tsx), clicking a row opens the edit modal (`onSelect` is really "edit"), and the header has no checkbox column.
3. **A bulk-action button.** The other tables have a "N selected" dropdown built on the shared `SelectedItemsButton` from [table.tsx](components/table.tsx), for example [SelectedTagsButton.tsx](components/tags/SelectedTagsButton.tsx) and `SelectedTransactionsButton`. Schedules has no equivalent.
4. **Actions on one schedule at a time.** Each action is a per-row menu item that calls `onAction(name, id)` with a single id ([index.tsx:51-82](components/schedules/index.tsx#L51-L82)). The server methods (`schedule/delete`, `schedule/skip-next-date`, `schedule/post-transaction`, `schedule/update`) also take one id each. Rules, by contrast, has a batch method, `rule-delete-all`. For schedules you'd either loop over the selected ids on the client or add batch server methods, so a bulk action can be undone in one step.

**Things specific to schedules:**
- **Completed schedules.** They're filtered behind a "Show completed schedules" row, and acceptance criterion 6 says they can't be bulk-edited. So selection has to exclude them, and that placeholder row isn't a real schedule.
- **Actions that depend on status.** "Restart" only appears for completed schedules; skip and complete are hidden for them. The bulk menu needs a rule for selections that mix statuses.
- **Reuse elsewhere.** `SchedulesTable` is also rendered in [ScheduleLink.tsx:140](components/schedules/ScheduleLink.tsx#L140) as a `minimal` picker, so checkboxes should be optional (off in minimal mode).

Short version: schedules has all the per-row actions already. What's missing is the selection layer (the provider, row and header checkboxes, and a bulk button), plus a decision on whether to batch the server calls.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 01:25:56Z)**_

## Scope

This is a medium change, and most of it is frontend wiring using pieces that already exist. Roughly 3–4 files change and about 150–300 lines.

| Area | Change | Size |
|---|---|---|
| [schedules/index.tsx](components/schedules/index.tsx) | Add `useSelected` and `<SelectedProvider>`, put the bulk button in the top bar, add a bulk version of `onAction` | Small to medium |
| [SchedulesTable.tsx](components/schedules/SchedulesTable.tsx) | Add a `SelectCell` to each row and a select-all cell to the header, hidden in `minimal` mode | Small |
| New `SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx` | Copy [SelectedTagsButton.tsx](components/tags/SelectedTagsButton.tsx) and swap in the schedule actions | Small |
| Server (optional) | Batch versions of delete, skip, complete and post | Medium, only if you choose that option below |
| Tests | Unit or e2e test for selecting rows and running a bulk action | Small to medium |

You don't need new UI components, since the checkbox, select-all and "N selected" button all already exist in `table.tsx`.

## Design choices

**1. How bulk actions run**
- **A. Loop on the client.** Call the existing single-schedule action once for each selected id. This is the least work, but undo then reverses one schedule at a time instead of the whole batch.
- **B. Add batch server methods**, such as `schedule/delete-all`, following the existing `rule-delete-all`. This means more work, but a single undo reverses the whole bulk action, and the data doesn't refresh once per schedule.
- I'd suggest starting with A and moving to B if one-at-a-time undo turns out to be a problem.

**2. Completed schedules**
- **A. Hide the checkbox on completed rows**, so they can never be selected.
- **B. Allow selecting them but disable the actions** that don't apply.
- The issue says completed schedules can't be bulk-edited, so A is the simplest fit. Select-all should also skip completed rows and the "Show completed" row.

**3. Mixed selections**

If you go with 2A, every selected schedule is active, so every action applies and you can skip this decision. Under 2B you'd need to decide whether to disable actions or only apply them where they're valid.

**4. Where the bulk button goes**
- **A. Top bar, left of the search box.** This matches Rules, Payees and Tags.
- **B. Bottom, next to "Add new schedule".**
- A is consistent with the rest of the app and answers one of the issue's open questions.

**5. Clicking a row**

Today clicking a row opens the edit dialog. Keep that, and only change selection when the checkbox is clicked, the same as Rules.

**6. Confirming deletes**

You could ask for confirmation before a bulk delete (e.g., "Delete 5 schedules?"), or rely on undo the way the other tables do. Relying on undo is consistent with the rest of the app, but a confirmation is a reasonable safety net if you go with 1A, where undo is per schedule.

## What I'd do

Client loop, checkboxes only on active schedules, button in the top bar, row click unchanged. That gives you the smallest change that meets every acceptance criterion, and you can add batch server methods later.

```text
type Actions = 'rename-tag' | 'delete-tags' | 'hide-tags' | 'unhide-tags';

type SelectedTagsButtonProps = {
  onRename: (id: TagEntity['id']) => void;
};

export function SelectedTagsButton({ onRename }: SelectedTagsButtonProps) {
  const dispatch = useSelectedDispatch();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const selectedItems = useSelectedItems();
  const { mutate: deleteTags } = useDeleteTagsMutation();
  const { mutate: hideTags } = useHideTagsMutation();
  const { mutate: unhideTags } = useUnhideTagsMutation();

  async function handleDelete(tagIds: string[]) {
    deleteTags(
      { ids: tagIds },
      { onSuccess: () => dispatch({ type: 'select-none' }) },
    );
  }

  // The closing menu restores focus to its trigger, so clear the selection
  // (which unmounts this button) and open the editor once that has settled
  function startRename(id: TagEntity['id']) {
    dispatch({ type: 'select-none' });
    requestAnimationFrame(() => onRename(id));
  }

  function handleSelect(name: Actions, tagIds: string[]) {
    if (name === 'rename-tag') {
      startRename(tagIds[0]);
    } else if (name === 'delete-tags') {
      void handleDelete(tagIds);
    } else if (name === 'hide-tags') {
      hideTags({ ids: [...tagIds] });
    } else if (name === 'unhide-tags') {
      unhideTags({ ids: [...tagIds] });
    } else {
      console.error('Unhandled action', name);
    }
  }

  const enabled = !!selectedItems.size;
  // Renaming edits a single row, so it is only offered for one selected tag
  const isSingleSelection = selectedItems.size === 1;
  useHotkeys('r', () => startRename([...selectedItems][0]), {
    enabled: isSingleSelection,
  });
  useHotkeys('d', () => handleDelete([...selectedItems]), { enabled });
  useHotkeys('h', () => hideTags({ ids: [...selectedItems] }), { enabled });
  useHotkeys('u', () => unhideTags({ ids: [...selectedItems] }), { enabled });

  return (
    <SelectedItemsButton<Actions>
      id="selected-tags"
      name={c => `${c} Tags`}
      items={[
        ...(isSingleSelection
          ? [
              {
                name: 'rename-tag',
                text: t('Rename'),
                key: 'R',
              } satisfies MenuItemObject<Actions>,
            ]
          : []),
        { name: 'delete-tags', text: t('Delete'), key: 'D' },
        { name: 'hide-tags', text: t('Hide'), key: 'H' },
        { name: 'unhide-tags', text: t('Unhide'), key: 'U' },
      ]}
      onSelect={handleSelect}
    />
  );
}
```

```text
export function useSelected<T extends Item>(
  name: string,
  items: T[],
  initialSelectedIds: string[],
  selectAllFilter?: (item: T) => boolean,
) {
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(
    (state: SelectedState, action: Actions) => {
      switch (action.type) {
        case 'select': {
          const { selectedRange } = state;
          const selectedItems = new Set(state.selectedItems);
          const { id, isRangeSelect } = action;

          if (isRangeSelect && selectedRange) {
            const idx = items.findIndex(p => p.id === id);
            const startIdx = items.findIndex(p => p.id === selectedRange.start);
            const endIdx = items.findIndex(p => p.id === selectedRange.end);
            let range: Range<number>;
            let deleteUntil: Range<number>;

            if (endIdx === -1) {
              range = { start: startIdx, end: idx };
            } else if (endIdx < startIdx) {
              if (idx <= startIdx) {
                range = { start: startIdx, end: idx };

                if (idx > endIdx) {
                  deleteUntil = { start: idx - 1, end: endIdx };
                }
              } else {
                // Switching directions
                range = { start: endIdx, end: idx };
              }
            } else {
              if (idx >= startIdx) {
                range = { start: startIdx, end: idx };

                if (idx < endIdx) {
                  deleteUntil = { start: idx + 1, end: endIdx };
                }
              } else {
                // Switching directions
                range = { start: endIdx, end: idx };
              }
            }

            iterateRange(range, i => selectedItems.add(items[i].id));

            if (deleteUntil) {
              iterateRange(deleteUntil, i => selectedItems.delete(items[i].id));
            }

            return {
              ...state,
              selectedItems,
              selectedRange: {
                start: items[range.start].id,
                end: items[range.end].id,
              },
            };
          } else {
            let range = null;
            if (!selectedItems.delete(id)) {
              selectedItems.add(id);
              range = { start: id, end: null };
            }

            return {
              ...state,
              selectedItems,
              selectedRange: range,
            };
          }
        }

        case 'select-none':
          return { ...state, selectedItems: new Set<string>() };

        case 'select-all':
          let selectedItems: string[] = [];
          if (action.ids && items && selectAllFilter) {
            const idsToInclude = new Set(
              items.filter(selectAllFilter).map(item => item.id),
            );
            selectedItems = action.ids.filter(id => idsToInclude.has(id));
          } else if (items && selectAllFilter) {
            selectedItems = items.filter(selectAllFilter).map(item => item.id);
          } else {
            selectedItems = action.ids || items.map(item => item.id);
          }
          return {
            ...state,
            selectedItems: new Set(selectedItems),
            selectedRange:
              action.ids && action.ids.length === 1
                ? { start: action.ids[0], end: null }
                : null,
          };

        default:
          throw new Error('Unexpected action: ' + JSON.stringify(action));
      }
    },
    null,
    () => ({
      selectedItems: new Set<string>(initialSelectedIds || []),
      selectedRange:
        initialSelectedIds && initialSelectedIds.length === 1
          ? { start: initialSelectedIds[0], end: null }
          : null,
    }),
  );

  const prevItems = useRef(items);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (state.selectedItems.size > 0) {
      // We need to make sure there are no ids in the selection that
      // aren't valid anymore. This happens if the item has been
      // deleted or otherwise removed from the current view. We do
      // this by cross-referencing the current selection with the
      // available item ids
      //
      // This effect may run multiple times while items is updated, we
      // need to make sure that we don't remove selected ids until the
      // items array *actually* changes. A component may render with
      // new `items` arrays that are the same, just fresh instances, but
      // we need to wait until the actual array changes. This solves
      // the case where undo-ing adds back items, but we remove the
      // selected item too early (because the component rerenders
      // multiple times)

      const ids = new Set(items.map(item => item.id));
      const isSame =
        prevItems.current.length === items.length &&
        prevItems.current.every(item => ids.has(item.id));

      if (!isSame) {
        const selected = [...state.selectedItems];
        const filtered = selected.filter(id => ids.has(id));

        // If the selected items has changed, update the selection
        if (selected.length !== filtered.length) {
          dispatch({ type: 'select-all', ids: filtered });
        }
      }
    }

    prevItems.current = items;
  }, [items, state.selectedItems]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const prevState = undo.getUndoState('selectedItems');
    undo.setUndoState('selectedItems', { name, items: state.selectedItems });
    return () => undo.setUndoState('selectedItems', prevState);
  }, [name, state.selectedItems]);

  useEffect(() => {
    function onUndo({ messages, undoTag }: UndoState) {
      const tagged = undo.getTaggedState(undoTag);

      const deletedIds = new Set(
        messages
          .filter(msg => msg.column === 'tombstone' && msg.value === 1)
          .map(msg => msg.row),
      );

      if (tagged?.selectedItems?.name === name) {
        dispatch({
          type: 'select-all',
          // Coerce the Set into an array
          ids: [...tagged.selectedItems.items].filter(
            id => !deletedIds.has(id),
          ),
        });
      }
    }

    const lastUndoEvent = undo.getUndoState('undoEvent');
    if (lastUndoEvent) {
      onUndo(lastUndoEvent);
    }

    return listen('undo-event', onUndo);
  }, [name]);

  return {
    items: state.selectedItems,
    dispatch,
  };
}

const SelectedDispatch = createContext<(action: Actions) => void>(null);
const SelectedItems = createContext<Set<string>>(null);

export function useSelectedDispatch() {
  return useContext(SelectedDispatch);
}

export function useSelectedItems() {
  return useContext(SelectedItems);
}

type SelectedProviderProps<T extends Item> = {
  instance: ReturnType<typeof useSelected<T>>;
  fetchAllIds?: () => Promise<string[]>;
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function SelectedProvider<T extends Item>({
  instance,
  fetchAllIds,
  children,
}: SelectedProviderProps<T>) {
  const { items: instanceItems, dispatch: instanceDispatch } = instance;
  const latestItems = useRef(instanceItems);
  latestItems.current = instanceItems;

  const dispatch = useCallback(
    async (action: Actions) => {
      if (action.type === 'select-all') {
        if (latestItems.current && latestItems.current.size > 0) {
          return instanceDispatch({
            type: 'select-none',
            isRangeSelect: action.isRangeSelect,
          });
        } else {
          if (fetchAllIds) {
            return instanceDispatch({
              type: 'select-all',
              ids: await fetchAllIds(),
              isRangeSelect: action.isRangeSelect,
            });
          }
          return instanceDispatch({
            type: 'select-all',
            isRangeSelect: action.isRangeSelect,
          });
        }
      }
      return instanceDispatch(action);
    },
    [instanceDispatch, fetchAllIds],
  );

  return (
    <SelectedItems.Provider value={instance.items}>
      <SelectedDispatch.Provider value={dispatch}>
        {children}
      </SelectedDispatch.Provider>
    </SelectedItems.Provider>
```

```markdown
# Plan: Bulk actions on the Schedules page (issue #65)

## Context
Most tables in Actual (Rules, Payees, Tags, Transactions) let you tick rows and run one action on all of them. Schedules can only be changed one row at a time through the row's "⋯" menu. Issue #65 asks for checkboxes, a select-all checkbox, and a bulk menu offering the same actions as the row menu. Completed schedules must not be bulk-editable.

Decisions already made:
- Run bulk actions with a loop on the client. No new server methods.
- Don't show a checkbox on completed rows.
- Put the bulk button in the top bar, matching the "N Tags" button on the Tags page.
- Clicking a row still opens the edit modal.
- Keyboard shortcuts are out of scope, per the issue.

## Existing pieces to reuse
- `useSelected(name, items, [])`, `SelectedProvider`, `useSelectedDispatch` and `useSelectedItems` in [hooks/useSelected.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useSelected.tsx). The provider already handles select-all/none toggling, shift-click range selection, dropping selected ids that disappear from `items`, and restoring the selection on undo.
- `SelectCell` and `SelectedItemsButton` in [components/table.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/table.tsx). `SelectCell` calls `stopPropagation`, so ticking a box won't open the edit modal.
- Reference implementation (Tags):
  - Page wiring: [ManageTags.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/ManageTags.tsx)
  - Header checkbox: [TagsHeader.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagsHeader.tsx)
  - Row checkbox: [TagRow.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagRow.tsx)
  - Bulk button: [SelectedTagsButton.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/SelectedTagsButton.tsx)

## Key design point: what counts as "selectable"
Shift-click range selection and select-all both work on the `items` list passed to `useSelected`. That list must therefore be **only the visible, active schedules**: schedules matching the search filter, minus completed ones. This gives three behaviours without extra code:
- Select-all and shift-click can never pick up completed or filtered-out schedules.
- When a schedule is completed or deleted, it drops out of `items`, and `useSelected`'s cleanup effect removes it from the selection.
- Undo restores the previous selection.

The search filter currently lives inside `SchedulesTable`, but the page component needs the same filtered list. The plan moves the filter into a shared hook so both use the same logic.

## Changes

### 1. New `components/schedules/useFilteredSchedules.ts`
- Move the `filteredSchedules` `useMemo` out of `SchedulesTable` unchanged. It uses payees, accounts, `useFormat`, `useDateFormat` and the filter string.
- Signature: `useFilteredSchedules({ schedules, filter, statuses })`, returning `ScheduleEntity[]`.
- This is a new file, so it must be type-strict (no `@ts-strict-ignore`).

### 2. [SchedulesTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/SchedulesTable.tsx)
- Use `useFilteredSchedules` in place of the inline memo.
- **Header:** when `!minimal`, add a `SelectCell` before "Name", copied from `TagsHeader`:
  - `exposed`
  - `selected={selectedItems.size > 0}`
  - `onSelect` dispatches `select-all` with `isRangeSelect: e.shiftKey`
- **`ScheduleRow`:**
  - Read `useSelectedItems()` and `useSelectedDispatch()`, and derive `selected = selectedItems?.has(schedule.id)`.
  - Optional chaining is needed because the `minimal` table in `ScheduleLink` has no provider.
  - Add a local `hovered` state through `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`.
  - When `!minimal && !schedule.completed`, render a `SelectCell` as the first cell:
    - `exposed={hovered || selected}`
    - `onSelect` dispatches `{ type: 'select', id, isRangeSelect: e.shiftKey }`
  - When `!minimal && schedule.completed`, render an empty `<Field width={20} />` so the columns stay aligned.
  - When a row is selected, use `theme.tableRowBackgroundHighlight` and `theme.tableBorderSelected`, as `TagRow` and `RuleRow` do.
  - The row's `onClick` (open the edit modal) stays as it is.
- Minimal mode (used by [ScheduleLink.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/ScheduleLink.tsx)) gets no checkboxes. Its behaviour doesn't change.

### 3. [schedules/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/index.tsx)
- Move the body of the `switch` in `onAction` into a module-level `async function runScheduleAction(name, id)`. The single-row `onAction` calls it, and so does the bulk button.
- Compute the selectable list: `useFilteredSchedules({ schedules, filter, statuses }).filter(s => !s.completed)`.
- Create the selection with `const selectedInst = useSelected('schedules', selectable, [])`.
- Wrap the page in `<SelectedProvider instance={selectedInst}>`.
- Put `<SelectedSchedulesButton onAction={runScheduleAction} />` in the top bar next to `<Search>`, matching the layout on ManageTags.

### 4. New `components/schedules/SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx`
This is modelled on `SelectedTagsButton`, without hotkeys.
- Uses `SelectedItemsButton<Action>` with:
```

```text
## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Bulk actions on the Schedules page (issue #65)

## Context
Most tables in Actual (Rules, Payees, Tags, Transactions) let you tick rows and run one action on all of them. Schedules can only be changed one row at a time through the row's "⋯" menu. Issue #65 asks for checkboxes, a select-all checkbox, and a bulk menu offering the same actions as the row menu. Completed schedules must not be bulk-editable.

Decisions already made:
- Run bulk actions with a loop on the client. No new server methods.
- Don't show a checkbox on completed rows.
- Put the bulk button in the top bar, matching the "N Tags" button on the Tags page.
- Clicking a row still opens the edit modal.
- Keyboard shortcuts are out of scope, per the issue.

## Existing pieces to reuse
- `useSelected(name, items, [])`, `SelectedProvider`, `useSelectedDispatch` and `useSelectedItems` in [hooks/useSelected.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useSelected.tsx). The provider already handles select-all/none toggling, shift-click range selection, dropping selected ids that disappear from `items`, and restoring the selection on undo.
- `SelectCell` and `SelectedItemsButton` in [components/table.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/table.tsx). `SelectCell` calls `stopPropagation`, so ticking a box won't open the edit modal.
- Reference implementation (Tags):
  - Page wiring: [ManageTags.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/ManageTags.tsx)
  - Header checkbox: [TagsHeader.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagsHeader.tsx)
  - Row checkbox: [TagRow.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/TagRow.tsx)
  - Bulk button: [SelectedTagsButton.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/tags/SelectedTagsButton.tsx)

## Key design point: what counts as "selectable"
Shift-click range selection and select-all both work on the `items` list passed to `useSelected`. That list must therefore be **only the visible, active schedules**: schedules matching the search filter, minus completed ones. This gives three behaviours without extra code:
- Select-all and shift-click can never pick up completed or filtered-out schedules.
- When a schedule is completed or deleted, it drops out of `items`, and `useSelected`'s cleanup effect removes it from the selection.
- Undo restores the previous selection.

The search filter currently lives inside `SchedulesTable`, but the page component needs the same filtered list. The plan moves the filter into a shared hook so both use the same logic.

## Changes

### 1. New `components/schedules/useFilteredSchedules.ts`
- Move the `filteredSchedules` `useMemo` out of `SchedulesTable` unchanged. It uses payees, accounts, `useFormat`, `useDateFormat` and the filter string.
- Signature: `useFilteredSchedules({ schedules, filter, statuses })`, returning `ScheduleEntity[]`.
- This is a new file, so it must be type-strict (no `@ts-strict-ignore`).

### 2. [SchedulesTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/SchedulesTable.tsx)
- Use `useFilteredSchedules` in place of the inline memo.
- **Header:** when `!minimal`, add a `SelectCell` before "Name", copied from `TagsHeader`:
  - `exposed`
  - `selected={selectedItems.size > 0}`
  - `onSelect` dispatches `select-all` with `isRangeSelect: e.shiftKey`
- **`ScheduleRow`:**
  - Read `useSelectedItems()` and `useSelectedDispatch()`, and derive `selected = selectedItems?.has(schedule.id)`.
  - Optional chaining is needed because the `minimal` table in `ScheduleLink` has no provider.
  - Add a local `hovered` state through `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`.
  - When `!minimal && !schedule.completed`, render a `SelectCell` as the first cell:
    - `exposed={hovered || selected}`
    - `onSelect` dispatches `{ type: 'select', id, isRangeSelect: e.shiftKey }`
  - When `!minimal && schedule.completed`, render an empty `<Field width={20} />` so the columns stay aligned.
  - When a row is selected, use `theme.tableRowBackgroundHighlight` and `theme.tableBorderSelected`, as `TagRow` and `RuleRow` do.
  - The row's `onClick` (open the edit modal) stays as it is.
- Minimal mode (used by [ScheduleLink.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/ScheduleLink.tsx)) gets no checkboxes. Its behaviour doesn't change.

### 3. [schedules/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/index.tsx)
- Move the body of the `switch` in `onAction` into a module-level `async function runScheduleAction(name, id)`. The single-row `onAction` calls it, and so does the bulk button.
- Compute the selectable list: `useFilteredSchedules({ schedules, filter, statuses }).filter(s => !s.completed)`.
- Create the selection with `const selectedInst = useSelected('schedules', selectable, [])`.
- Wrap the page in `<SelectedProvider instance={selectedInst}>`.
- Put `<SelectedSchedulesButton onAction={runScheduleAction} />` in the top bar next to `<Search>`, matching the layout on ManageTags.

### 4. New `components/schedules/SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx`

  - After `complete` or `delete`, dispatches `select-none` so the button disappears. The cleanup effect would also handle this.
```

```typescript
import { useMemo } from 'react';

import { format as monthUtilFormat } from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
import { getNormalisedString } from '@actual-app/core/shared/normalisation';
import { getScheduledAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/schedules';
import type { ScheduleStatuses } from '@actual-app/core/shared/schedules';
import type { ScheduleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { useAccounts } from '#hooks/useAccounts';
import { useDateFormat } from '#hooks/useDateFormat';
import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';
import { usePayees } from '#hooks/usePayees';

type UseFilteredSchedulesProps = {
  schedules: readonly ScheduleEntity[];
  filter: string;
  statuses: ScheduleStatuses;
};

export function useFilteredSchedules({
  schedules,
  filter,
  statuses,
}: UseFilteredSchedulesProps): readonly ScheduleEntity[] {
  const format = useFormat();
  const dateFormat = useDateFormat() || 'MM/dd/yyyy';
  const { data: payees = [] } = usePayees();
  const { data: accounts = [] } = useAccounts();

  return useMemo(() => {
    if (!filter) {
      return schedules;
    }
    const filterIncludes = (str: string | null | undefined) =>
      str
        ? getNormalisedString(str).includes(getNormalisedString(filter)) ||
          getNormalisedString(filter).includes(getNormalisedString(str))
        : false;

    return schedules.filter(schedule => {
      const payee = payees.find(p => schedule._payee === p.id);
      const account = accounts.find(a => schedule._account === a.id);
      const amount = getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount);
      let amountStr = '';
      if (schedule._amountOp === 'isbetween') {
        amountStr = '±';
      } else if (schedule._amountOp === 'isapprox') {
        amountStr = '~';
      }
      amountStr +=
        (amount > 0 ? '+' : '') + format(Math.abs(amount || 0), 'financial');
      const dateStr = schedule.next_date
        ? monthUtilFormat(schedule.next_date, dateFormat)
        : null;

      return (
        filterIncludes(schedule.name) ||
        filterIncludes(payee && payee.name) ||
        filterIncludes(account && account.name) ||
        filterIncludes(amountStr) ||
        filterIncludes(statuses.get(schedule.id)) ||
        filterIncludes(dateStr)
      );
    });
  }, [payees, accounts, schedules, filter, statuses, format, dateFormat]);
}
```

```typescript
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';

import type { ScheduleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { SelectedItemsButton } from '#components/table';
import { useSelectedDispatch } from '#hooks/useSelected';

import type { ScheduleItemAction } from './SchedulesTable';

// Restart only applies to completed schedules, which can't be selected
type Actions = Exclude<ScheduleItemAction, 'restart'>;

type SelectedSchedulesButtonProps = {
  onAction: (name: Actions, id: ScheduleEntity['id']) => Promise<void>;
};

export function SelectedSchedulesButton({
  onAction,
}: SelectedSchedulesButtonProps) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const dispatch = useSelectedDispatch();

  async function handleSelect(name: Actions, scheduleIds: string[]) {
    for (const id of scheduleIds) {
      await onAction(name, id);
    }

    // Completed and deleted schedules leave the selectable list
    if (name === 'complete' || name === 'delete') {
      dispatch({ type: 'select-none' });
    }
  }

  return (
    <SelectedItemsButton<Actions>
      id="selected-schedules"
      name={count => t('{{count}} schedules', { count })}
      items={[
        { name: 'post-transaction', text: t('Post transaction') },
        { name: 'post-transaction-today', text: t('Post transaction today') },
        { name: 'skip', text: t('Skip next scheduled date') },
        { name: 'complete', text: t('Complete') },
        { name: 'delete', text: t('Delete') },
      ]}
      onSelect={(name, ids) => void handleSelect(name, ids)}
    />
  );
}
```

```text
import type { Locator, Page } from '@playwright/test';

import { ScheduleEditModal } from './schedule-edit-modal';

export class SchedulesPage {
  readonly page: Page;
  readonly addNewScheduleButton: Locator;
  readonly schedulesTableRow: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.page = page;

    this.addNewScheduleButton = this.page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Add new schedule',
    });
    this.schedulesTableRow = this.page.getByTestId('table').getByTestId('row');
  }

  /**
   * Open the schedule edit modal.
   */
  async addNewSchedule() {
    await this.addNewScheduleButton.click();

    return new ScheduleEditModal(this.page.getByTestId('schedule-edit-modal'));
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve the row element for the nth-schedule.
   * 0-based index
   */
  getNthScheduleRow(index: number) {
    return this.schedulesTableRow.nth(index);
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve the data for the nth-schedule.
   * 0-based index
   */
  getNthSchedule(index: number) {
    const row = this.getNthScheduleRow(index);

    return {
      payee: row.getByTestId('payee'),
      account: row.getByTestId('account'),
      date: row.getByTestId('date'),
      status: row.getByTestId('status'),
      amount: row.getByTestId('amount'),
    };
  }

  /**
   * Create a transaction for the nth-schedule.
   * 0-based index
   */
  async postNthSchedule(index: number) {
    await this._performNthAction(index, 'Post transaction today');
  }

  /**
   * Complete the nth-schedule.
   * 0-based index
   */
  async completeNthSchedule(index: number) {
    await this._performNthAction(index, 'Complete');
  }

  async _performNthAction(index: number, actionName: string | RegExp) {
    const row = this.getNthScheduleRow(index);
    const actions = row.getByTestId('actions');

    await actions.getByRole('button').click();
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: actionName }).click();
  }

  async rightClickNthSchedule(index: number) {
    await this.getNthScheduleRow(index).click({ button: 'right' });
  }
}
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';

import { expect, test } from './fixtures';
import { ConfigurationPage } from './page-models/configuration-page';
import { Navigation } from './page-models/navigation';
import type { SchedulesPage } from './page-models/schedules-page';

test.describe('Schedules', () => {
  let page: Page;
  let navigation: Navigation;
  let schedulesPage: SchedulesPage;
  let configurationPage: ConfigurationPage;

  test.beforeEach(async ({ browser }) => {
    page = await browser.newPage();
    navigation = new Navigation(page);
    configurationPage = new ConfigurationPage(page);

    await page.goto('/');
    await configurationPage.createTestFile();

    schedulesPage = await navigation.goToSchedulesPage();
  });

  test.afterEach(async () => {
    await page?.close();
  });

  test('checks the page visuals', async () => {
    await expect(page).toMatchThemeScreenshots();
  });

  test('creates a new schedule, posts the transaction and later completes it', async () => {
    const scheduleEditModal = await schedulesPage.addNewSchedule();
    await scheduleEditModal.fill({
      payee: 'Home Depot',
      account: 'HSBC',
      amount: 25,
    });
    await scheduleEditModal.add();

    const schedule = schedulesPage.getNthSchedule(2);
    await expect(schedule.payee).toHaveText('Home Depot');
    await expect(schedule.account).toHaveText('HSBC');
    await expect(schedule.amount).toHaveText('~25.00');
    await expect(schedule.status).toHaveText('Due');
    await expect(page).toMatchThemeScreenshots();

    await schedulesPage.postNthSchedule(2);
    await expect(schedulesPage.getNthSchedule(2).status).toHaveText('Paid');
    await expect(page).toMatchThemeScreenshots();

    // Go to transactions page
    const accountPage = await navigation.goToAccountPage('HSBC');
    const transaction = accountPage.getNthTransaction(0);
    await expect(transaction.payee).toHaveText('Home Depot');
    await expect(transaction.category).toHaveText('Categorize');
    await expect(transaction.debit).toHaveText('25.00');
    await expect(transaction.credit).toHaveText('');

    const icon = transaction.payee.getByTestId('schedule-icon');
    await icon.hover();
    await expect(page).toMatchThemeScreenshots();

    // go to rules page
    const rulesPage = await navigation.goToRulesPage();
    await rulesPage.searchFor('Home Depot');
    const rule = rulesPage.getNthRule(0);
    await expect(rule.actions).toHaveText([
      'link schedule Home Depot (2017-01-01)',
    ]);
    await expect(rule.conditions).toHaveText([

  test('shows a scheduled split transfer in its destination account', async () => {
    await page.evaluate(async () => {
      const $send = (
        window as unknown as {
          $send: <T>(type: string, args?: unknown) => Promise<T>;
        }
      ).$send;
      const query = <T>(
        table: string,
        filterExpressions: unknown[],
        selectExpressions: string[],
      ) =>
        $send<{ data: T[] }>('query', {
          table,
          tableOptions: {},
          filterExpressions,
          selectExpressions,
          groupExpressions: [],
          orderExpressions: [],
          calculation: false,
          rawMode: false,
          withDead: false,
          validateRefs: true,
          limit: null,
          offset: null,
        });

      const {
        data: [destinationAccount],
      } = await query<{ id: string }>(
        'accounts',
        [{ name: 'Ally Savings' }],
        ['id'],
      );
      const {
        data: [destinationPayee],
      } = await query<{ id: string }>(
        'payees',
        [{ transfer_acct: destinationAccount.id }],
        ['id'],
      );
      const {
        data: [schedule],
      } = await query<{ rule: string }>(
        'schedules',
        [{ name: 'Phone bills' }],
        ['rule'],
      );
      const rule = await $send<{
        actions: unknown[];
        conditions: unknown[];
        conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
        id: string;
        stage: 'pre' | 'post' | null;
      }>('rule-get', { id: schedule.rule });

      await $send('rule-update', {
        ...rule,
        actions: [
          ...rule.actions,
          {
            op: 'set-split-amount',
            value: -7_000,
            options: { splitIndex: 1, method: 'fixed-amount' },
          },
          {
            op: 'set-split-amount',
            value: null,
            options: { splitIndex: 2, method: 'remainder' },
          },
          {
            op: 'set',
            field: 'payee',
            value: destinationPayee.id,
            options: { splitIndex: 2 },
          },
        ],
      });
    });

    const destinationAccountPage =
      await navigation.goToAccountPage('Ally Savings');
    const previewTransfer = destinationAccountPage.transactionTableRow.filter({
      has: page.getByTestId('schedule-icon'),
      hasText: 'Bank of America',
    });

    await expect(previewTransfer).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(previewTransfer.getByTestId('category')).toContainText('Due');
    await expect(previewTransfer.getByTestId('debit')).toHaveText('');
    await expect(previewTransfer.getByTestId('credit')).toHaveText('50.00');
  });

  test('creates two new schedules, posts both transactions and later completes one', async () => {
    // Adding two schedules with the same payee and account and amount, mimicking two different subscriptions
    let scheduleEditModal = await schedulesPage.addNewSchedule();
    await scheduleEditModal.fill({

    const schedule = schedulesPage.getNthSchedule(2);

    const schedule2 = schedulesPage.getNthSchedule(3);

    await schedulesPage.postNthSchedule(2);
```

<pasted_content id="3ea8">
## Description

Fixes custom reports still counting a subcategory after it's unchecked in the category list (#100). Before this change, unchecking a subcategory didn't change the report: its amount stayed in the parent category's total. If the parent was unchecked and a subcategory was left checked, the subcategory's amount showed up under the parent's name.

- **`subcategories.ts`:**
  - Custom reports now apply the category checkbox filter exactly as written. Before, any parent in the filter had all of its subcategories added back, so unchecked ones were still fetched.
  - A subcategory only rolls into its parent's row when both are checked. One checked without its parent is shown as its own row.
- **`custom-spreadsheet.ts` / `grouped-spreadsheet.ts`:** both use the new filter handling and the narrowed roll-up. This covers every graph type (Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Table), Budgeted mode and dashboard widgets.
- **`showActivity.ts`:** clicking a parent's bar or row keeps the report's category filter as written, so the transaction list leaves out unchecked subcategories and matches the row.
- **`CustomReport.tsx`:** the check for filters too complex for the checkboxes now comes from a shared helper, so the checkboxes and the report read the filter the same way.

Report totals now stay correct whichever parents and subcategories are checked.

## Design Decisions

- **Keep subcategories rolled into the parent's bar, and only fix which ones are included.** The issue also asks to see how much each subcategory contributes. This PR doesn't change the graphs, so it stays small and fixes the incorrect totals first. Two alternatives were considered:
  1. **Show each subcategory as its own bar.**
     - Pros: fits every graph type.
     - Cons: needs a new saved report option (database migration, report types, sidebar toggle, dashboard widgets), plus click-through changes in five graph components. Without a toggle it would change how every existing report looks.
     - Status: left as a follow-up.
  2. **Split each parent's bar into coloured segments, one per subcategory.**
     - Pros: looks good for Bar, and possibly Donut.
     - Cons: doesn't carry over to Stacked Bar (which already stacks categories over time), Line or Area, so behaviour would be inconsistent across graph types. Also needs per-segment data, colours, tooltips, legend and click handling, and new visual regression snapshots. It wouldn't fix the totals on its own either; this PR's filter change is still needed underneath.
- **The checkbox filter is applied as written instead of expanding parents.** Ticking a parent already ticks all its subcategories, so the filter already lists exactly what's checked. Expanding it was what added unchecked subcategories back. Other category filters, and other reports such as Spending and Cash Flow, still include a parent's subcategories.
- **A subcategory checked without its parent gets its own row.** Showing it under a parent the user unchecked was misleading. Hiding it would have dropped data the user asked for.
- **The click-through query isn't changed.** It still asks for the parent and all its subcategories, combined with the report's filter. Because the filter is now applied as written, unchecked subcategories drop out without changing every graph's click handler.

## UML Diagram

## Tech Debt

**Introduced**
- In custom reports, a single typed filter like `Category is Food` now covers Food only, not its subcategories. This matches what the checkboxes already showed, but it differs from other reports, where the same filter includes subcategories.
- `useSelectedCategories` in `CustomReport.tsx` still has its own copy of the logic for reading the checkbox filter, separate from the new `getSelectedCategoryIds` helper. It wasn't merged because the two behave differently when the filter is too complex for the checkboxes.
- The issue's request to see each subcategory on its own is only partly met. The Table view nests subcategory rows under their parent, but the graphs still show one bar per parent.

**Encountered**
- Dashboard widgets don't pass the report's filters to the graphs (`GetCardData.tsx`), so clicking a bar in a widget ignores the report's filters.
- The checkbox list and the report filter bar share one condition, so a filter typed by hand and a checkbox selection can't be told apart.
- The report spreadsheet tests mock the database query, so the query results ignore the filters. Tests have to supply already-filtered rows themselves.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #100

- [ ] Release notes added (see link above)
- [ ] No obvious regressions in affected areas
- [ ] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed

Written for: reviewers of the issue #65 pull request, in the same format as your #100 description.

```markdown
## Description

Adds bulk actions to the Schedules page (#65). Before this change, schedules could only be changed one at a time through each row's "⋯" menu, unlike Rules, Payees, Tags and Transactions, which all let you tick rows and act on them together.

- **`SchedulesTable.tsx`:**
  - Each active schedule row has a checkbox, shown on hover or when the row is selected, and the header has a select-all checkbox. Selected rows are highlighted the same way as on the Rules and Tags pages.
  - Completed rows get an empty space in place of the checkbox, so the columns stay aligned.
  - Clicking a row still opens the schedule editor. Clicking the checkbox only changes the selection.
  - The compact table used by the schedule picker on transactions (`ScheduleLink`) has no checkboxes and is unchanged.
- **`SelectedSchedulesButton.tsx` (new):** an "N schedules" dropdown next to the search box, built on the shared `SelectedItemsButton`. It offers the same actions as a row's menu: Post transaction, Post transaction today, Skip next scheduled date, Complete and Delete. Restart is left out because it only applies to completed schedules.
- **`index.tsx`:**
  - The page is wrapped in a `SelectedProvider`. Only schedules that are visible and not completed can be selected.
  - The action handling moved into a shared `runScheduleAction` function, used by both the row menu and the bulk button.
- **`useFilteredSchedules.ts` (new):** the search filter moved out of `SchedulesTable` so the page and the table work from the same filtered list.
- **E2E:** new page-model helpers, plus tests for bulk skip, complete and delete, completed rows having no checkbox, select-all, and row click still opening the editor.

## Design Decisions

- **Bulk actions run in a loop on the client, calling the existing single-schedule action once per selected schedule.** This reuses the server methods the row menu already calls, so the behaviour of each action is unchanged and no `loot-core` code changes. One alternative was considered:
  1. **Edit all selected schedules at once with batch server methods** (e.g. `schedule/delete-all`, following the existing `rule-delete-all`).
     - Pros: one request per bulk action instead of one per schedule, the data refreshes once, and a single undo reverts the whole bulk action.
     - Cons: needs four new server methods with types and tests. Posting a transaction and skipping a date each run per-schedule logic (rules, next-date calculation) that would have to be restructured to run in a batch.
     - Status: left as a follow-up if undoing one schedule at a time proves to be a problem.
- **Completed schedules have no checkbox.** The issue says completed schedules can't be bulk-edited, and leaving out the checkbox enforces that without extra rules in the menu. One alternative was considered:
  1. **Let completed schedules be selected, and disable or hide the actions that don't apply to them**, offering Restart when only completed schedules are selected.
     - Pros: would also allow bulk restarting or deleting completed schedules.
     - Cons: editing completed schedules is out of scope for the issue. Mixed selections would need rules for which actions to show, and select-all would have to decide whether to include completed schedules hidden behind "Show completed schedules".
     - Status: not done.
- **Only visible, active schedules can be selected.** The selection is given only the schedules matching the search filter that aren't completed. Select-all and shift-click therefore never pick up hidden or completed schedules. A schedule that is completed or deleted also drops out of the selection on its own.
- **The bulk button sits in the top bar next to the search box**, matching the Tags, Rules and Payees pages.
- **Clicking a row still opens the editor.** The checkbox stops the click from reaching the row, as it does on the Rules page.
- **The selection is kept after Post and Skip, and cleared after Complete and Delete.** Posting or skipping can sensibly be repeated on the same schedules, while completed and deleted schedules can no longer be selected.
- **No keyboard shortcuts**, since the issue lists them as out of scope.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced**
- Each schedule in a bulk action is its own undo step, so undoing a bulk delete of five schedules takes five undos.
- If one schedule's action fails partway through a bulk action, the loop stops. Schedules before it have already been changed, and no error is shown, the same as when a single-row action fails today.
- The search filter now runs twice per render, once in the page to work out what can be selected and once in the table to show rows. Both use the same hook, so the results match.
- The action labels are written out in both the row menu and the bulk button.
- The new checkbox column changes the Schedules page screenshots, so the visual regression snapshots need regenerating.

**Encountered**
- Row checkboxes are revealed on hover, which redraws the cell when the pointer enters the row. In tests, a click that doesn't hover first is lost. The Tags and Rules tables reveal their checkboxes the same way. The new tests hover before clicking.
- The schedule edit modal's `add()` page-model helper doesn't wait for the modal to close, so tests that click the table right after adding a schedule have to wait for it themselves.
- `SchedulesTable.tsx` is still excluded from strict type checking (`@ts-strict-ignore`).
```
